Vocal input validation and dataset analysis¶

This notebook follows a real Vocadito recording through source inventory, technical validation, measured acoustic features and an accepted audio package. A singer or humming user does not need to enter note names or music theory.

The original file is preserved. Unsupported or unusable recordings receive a clear stop or rerecord request. Technical acceptance means the file can be processed; it does not certify musical correctness.

The two notebook sources are maintained in notebooks/. Saved executions preserve the full record. This notebook runs input checks and creates new technical fixtures only; it does not fit a model or run the shared extraction pipeline.

Processing objective¶

Use case: accept a short solo singing/humming recording, retain its original timing and identity, measure useful voice features, and expose a checked optional processing candidate to the user.

Flow: recording -> integrity and duration checks -> mono working copy -> pitch, confidence, boundaries and log-mel features -> accepted package or controlled stop.

Notebook 2 explains Vocadito/Jamendo preparation, the four-view Transformer method, real-data adaptation, measured input/output examples and the complete evaluation. Start the local interface with Run-System.ps1. Prepared downstream handoff stays off; cleaned or pitch-corrected candidates are separate outputs.

Evidence updated: 2026-10-18
Scope: solo singing/humming, WAV/FLAC, 0.25-20 seconds
Reference review: deferred_by_owner

4. Inspect performed pitch and uncertainty¶

Feature shapes: (455, 70) (455, 71)

Spikes and missing F0 may be analyzer errors. Performed F0 is not intended melody. Unvoiced frames are NaN in plots and masked zeros in model features. Provisional boundaries are heuristics. Frame-only inputs have 70 features; timing-boundary metadata adds the 71st.

Saved replay matches the current recording bytes and Phase 1 policy; it is not a new accuracy study.
This older replay does not record a source-code hash, so code-revision equivalence is unverified.

What this demonstrates: original retention, technical processing, controlled stops, accepted-only packaging, original timing and measured acoustics. Audio widgets aid playback; saved WAV hashes identify the actual artifacts.

Implemented and explained in notebook 2: real/synthetic preparation, four views, matched Transformers and losses, completed studies, numerical candidate verification, rollback and annotation-free live inference.

Still research requirements: independent reference suitability, stable real-singer recovery, preservation/acceptance calibration, the BPDR advantage, consented participant and blinded listening studies, downstream extraction benefit and a reserved final test. Research-ready examples remain zero. A verified numerical preview is not musical approval or prepared-audio adoption.
